bibl.title: Ultrawide‐Bandgap Semiconductors: Research Opportunities and Challenges

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors - AlGaN/AlN, diamond, Ga2O3 and cubic BN - and what stands between their theoretical advantage and a working device
span.quote: Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors, with bandgaps significantly wider than the 3.4 eV of GaN, represent an exciting and challenging new area of research in semiconductor materials, physics, devices, and applications.

span.label: which materials, physics and device problems must be solved before ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors can deliver the performance their bandgaps imply
span.quote: This article articulates the research challenges and opportunities identified in that second workshop and fleshed out in subsequent months, with the hope that it will help serve in the short term as a research agenda for the community, and in the long term as a catalyzing agent for the realization of the potential of UWBG semiconductor technology.

span.label: 26 numbered research opportunities and challenges, a re-derived table of reference material properties, and an explicit maturity assessment of each material system
span.quote: Throughout, we call out a set of especially important research opportunities and challenges, both scattered throughout the paper and compiled in summary in Section 5.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Despite such tremendous potential for revolutionary device performance improvement, UWBG semiconductors are immature. While some of the UWBG semiconductors have been a topic of research for a decade or two, only recently have there been demonstrations of devices, and even then only in a small number of laboratories around the world.

span.label: a nonlinear payoff: because the critical field scales as the square of the bandgap and the Baliga figure of merit as its cube, device performance scales as roughly the sixth power of bandgap
span.quote: The critical electric field, in turn, scales approximately as the square of the semiconductor bandgap, so the BFOM scales approximately as the sixth power of the semiconductor bandgap. In other words, moving from GaN to AlN gives an increase in bandgap by a factor of 1.8 ≈ 6.0 eV/3.4 eV, but a nonlinear increase in the BFOM of ≈ 34 ≈ (1.8)6.

span.label: a community workshop under AFOSR and NSF sponsorship, written up as a survey with a comprehensive re-survey of room-temperature material properties from the primary literature
span.term: a community workshop under AFOSR and NSF sponsorship, written up as a survey with a comprehensive re-survey of room-temperature material properties from the primary literature
span.quote: This article articulates the research challenges and opportunities identified in that second workshop and fleshed out in subsequent months, with the hope that it will help serve in the short term as a research agenda for the community, and in the long term as a catalyzing agent for the realization of the potential of UWBG semiconductor technology.

span.label: why a modest bandgap increase is worth a hard materials problem: the critical field goes as the square of the bandgap and the Baliga FOM as its cube, so GaN to AlN is 1.8x in bandgap and about 34x in figure of merit
span.quote: The critical electric field, in turn, scales approximately as the square of the semiconductor bandgap, so the BFOM scales approximately as the sixth power of the semiconductor bandgap. In other words, moving from GaN to AlN gives an increase in bandgap by a factor of 1.8 ≈ 6.0 eV/3.4 eV, but a nonlinear increase in the BFOM of ≈ 34 ≈ (1.8)6.

span.label: why doping gets harder as the gap widens - the formation energies of compensating defects DECREASE with increasing bandgap, so free carriers first rise with dopant concentration and then fall
span.quote: Third, there is a prevalent tendency of dopants in UWBG semiconductors to undergo compensation via impurities, native defects, or defect complexes. This tendency is illustrated in **Figure** **7** for n-type doping of AlGaN by Si. As Si concentration increases, free carrier concentrations initially increase, but then reach a maximum and decrease—a signature of compensation, where vacancies and their complexes determine the net free-carrier density. Such compensation is universal to all UWBG semiconductors, not just AlGaN, since in general the formation energies of compensating defects decrease with increasing bandgap.

span.label: a second doping obstacle: localized valence-band states, notably from first-row elements such as oxygen, let a hole trap itself in its own lattice distortion as a small polaron, suppressing mobility even where a shallow acceptor exists
span.quote: Second, the wide bandgaps of UWBG materials can make them prone to self-trapping of carriers. In particular, the localized nature of valence-band states derived from elements of the first row of the periodic table (notably oxygen) can lead to formation of small hole polarons, in which a hole is self-trapped due to lattice distortions.132 Even if suitable shallow acceptors could be identified, this tendency for carrier localization will suppress mobility.

span.label: the fundamental obstacle to gate insulators: a dielectric with a large bandgap tends to have a low dielectric constant and vice versa, so the high-k insulator a UWBG MOSFET wants may not exist
span.quote: The most fundamental obstacle is that any dielectric with a large bandgap will tend to have a low dielectric constant—and vice versa. This problem restricts the possibility of the high-k dielectrics desirable for realizing high-performance UWBG MOSFETs in the future, and is an extremely important research opportunity/challenge.

span.label: new physics that only appears here - when the bandgap exceeds the electron affinity, a carrier must have kinetic energy above the affinity to impact-ionise, so it momentarily occupies vacuum states before doing so
span.quote: Because the bandgaps of most UWBG materials are larger than the electron affinity, breakdown mechanisms such as the onset of the avalanche process by impact ionization require carriers in the conduction band to have a kinetic energy larger than the electron affinity. This implies the carrier momentarily spends time in vacuum states before causing impact ionization. This sort of physics is new and unique to UWBG semiconductors, and would have intriguing consequences for device design and operation.

span.label: why carrier confinement gets harder with a wider gap: the number of semiconductors and insulators with large enough band offsets DECREASES, and for AlN, BN and diamond few dielectrics are predicted to confine electrons at all
span.quote: As the bandgap of the semiconductor increases, the number of suitable semiconductors or insulators with large enough band offsets available for carrier confinement decreases. As illustrated in **Figure** **9**, the UWBG semiconductors have conduction bands that trend towards the vacuum level. There are few dielectric layers with a predicted band alignment that will confine electrons in AlN, BN or diamond.

span.label: every one of the three leading UWBG materials is poor on at least one of the three metrics that matter: AlN and Ga2O3 cannot be usefully p-doped, and diamond substrates are small or defective
span.quote: One can see that each of the three UWBG materials presently has poor performance in their states-of-the-art in at least one of the three important metrics: AlN and Ga2O3 cannot (or can only poorly) be p-doped; and diamond has limited size or relatively poor quality substrates.

span.label: the critical breakdown fields of AlN, BN, Ga2O3 and diamond - the property the whole case rests on - are yet to be accurately determined
span.quote: While critical breakdown fields in GaN have been measured59, 60 to be in excess of ≈4 MV cm−1, those in AlN, BN, Ga2O3, and diamond are yet to be accurately determined.

span.label: Ga2O3's thermal conductivity is one to two orders of magnitude below the other UWBG semiconductors, which the paper calls perhaps its single most serious weakness
span.quote: Second, Ga2O3 has poor thermal conductivity and therefore poor heat-dissipation capability. This low thermal conductivity is perhaps the single most serious potential weakness of Ga2O3 for power devices. The experimental thermal conductivity values of Ga2O3 fall in the range of ≈10–27 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature, which is one or two orders of magnitude lower than those of other UWBG semiconductors.

span.label: and p-type doping of Ga2O3 has never been reported, with hole self-trapping predicted from first principles
span.quote: First, in contrast to n-type material, there has been no report of successful p-type doping and thus of effective hole conduction in Ga2O3. Self-trapping of holes, which prohibits effective p-type conductivity due to the resultant low mobility, has been predicted by first-principles calculations.

span.label: AlN has no known acceptors at all, and only one postulated shallow donor
span.quote: Doping of AlN is still in its infancy, with no known acceptors available and sulfur postulated as the only likely shallow donor.

span.label: c-BN is the least mature of them, with substrates available only by the high-pressure high-temperature route
span.quote: c-BN is the least mature materials technology in this table, with substrates of c-BN now produced only by the high-pressure, high-temperature (HPHT) method that historically has produced most industrial diamonds.

span.label: the survey covers only the KNOWN applications, and the authors say plainly that the technology will create applications that do not yet exist
span.quote: However, we emphasize that we survey only the known applications—with the understanding that the new technology capabilities represented by UWBG semiconductors will surely create applications that do not yet exist.

span.label: extracting a critical field from a working device is unreliable because edge terminations cause premature breakdown - and the higher the voltage the more likely that is, so the measurement gets harder exactly where it matters most
span.quote: Extracting this critical field from a working power device is problematic, due to the possibility of premature breakdown associated with imperfect edge terminations—a possibility made more likely by the very high voltages enabled by UWBG semiconductors.

span.label: deep-level transient spectroscopy stops working on these materials because the traps are too deep and emission times too long - a standard characterisation technique defeated by the property under study
span.quote: For example, defect states in UWBG materials can be very deep in the gap, leading to excessively long carrier emission times, rendering techniques based on thermal emission of carriers such as deep-level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) ineffective.

span.label: and as devices shrink, optical thermometry becomes diffraction-limited, so a point-temperature measurement silently becomes a weighted average over a volume
span.quote: For example, the spatial resolution of any optical technique for local temperature measurement may become diffraction-limited. Thus, a technique that in a large device would be sufficient to measure a single “point” temperature might now measure a weighted average over a non-negligible volume.

span.label: TCAD device-modelling tools and physical models developed for silicon, applied to ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors
span.quote: Much can be borrowed from this legacy silicon TCAD, but there are significant challenges.

span.label: re-surveying the room-temperature material properties from the primary literature rather than reproducing the values in common use
span.note: eliminates: a comparison table built on numbers measured decades ago on material that would now be called highly defective - which is the stated reason the re-survey was necessary · outcome: held
span.quote: It was necessitated in part by the fact that many material properties in common use (even for GaN) were determined by measurements performed decades ago on material that was highly defective by today's standards.

span.label: projecting every material's critical field from GaN's measured value THROUGH THE SAME assumed device - a non-punched-through p+/n diode at a stated donor concentration
span.note: eliminates: materials being ranked on critical fields measured in different device geometries at different dopings, which the authors call ensuring a level playing field · outcome: held
span.quote: The second materials/device properties row reports projected bulk values of the critical electric field ( _E_ C) at avalanche breakdown for each UWBG material starting with AlN (the HEMT column is a measured result). The projection uses the experimentally derived _E_ C for GaN59 as the baseline (corrected for the updated values of mobility and permittivity in the table), as this is the highest known _E_ C for any GaN or SiC diode. These projections follow the method described in detail in Hollis and Kaplar,60 and, to ensure a level playing field for all materials, assume a non-punched-through p+/n diode having an ionized donor concentration of 1016 cm−3 in the n-region.

span.label: choosing the Hall-derived bulk drift mobility over values fitted to current-voltage characteristics, on the stated ground that the fits carry more assumptions
span.note: eliminates: a mobility chosen for convenience - AND THE AUTHORS BOUND THE STAKES rather than just declaring the choice: the critical field varies as the cube root of mobility, so the difference is small · outcome: held
span.quote: fits generally have more assumptions and uncertainties than direct Hall measurements, we chose to use the Hall-derived bulk drift mobility of 1000 to extract the critical field for GaN in row 2

span.label: flagging every table entry where the reported figure is a Hall mobility because the conversion factor to drift mobility is unknown for that material
span.note: eliminates: two different quantities being read down one column as if they were the same measurement · outcome: held
span.quote: Finally, in several instances in the table the reported mobilities are Hall mobilities, as the Hall conversion factor is unknown for those materials.

span.label: labelling the maturity verdict INFORMAL and printing its three sub-criteria as separate table rows
span.note: eliminates: a Mature/Immature label being read as a measurement - the inputs are beside it and a reader can disagree with the aggregation · outcome: held
span.quote: Finally, based on the current state-of-the-art values for their properties, we give an informal assessment of the maturity level of the various materials.

span.label: compiling all 26 research opportunities/challenges into a single numbered list in Section 5, having stated each where it arose
span.note: eliminates: an agenda that exists only as prose scattered through 42,000 words - the list is what makes the paper's claims about the field's gaps countable · outcome: held
span.quote: Throughout, we call out a set of especially important research opportunities and challenges, both scattered throughout the paper and compiled in summary in Section 5.

span.label: warning against importing default physical mechanisms from silicon TCAD, or extrapolating them past the range the legacy materials support
span.note: eliminates: a model that runs and converges on UWBG devices while computing silicon's physics - the paper then gives four specific ways it goes wrong · outcome: held
span.quote: Care must be taken not to borrow “default” physical mechanisms from silicon that are irrelevant for the UWBG materials in question, or that are extrapolated beyond the range (i.e., high temperatures or high electric fields) that legacy semiconducting materials support.

span.label: stating that standard characterisation assumptions, such as complete ionisation of dopants, may simply be untrue in these materials
span.note: eliminates: experimental results being interpreted through assumptions that hold for narrower-gap semiconductors and not here · outcome: held
span.quote: In general, great care must be taken in interpreting experimental results on UWBG semiconductors, since the assumptions typically made in characterization experiments on conventional semiconductor materials (e.g., complete ionization of dopants) may very well prove to be untrue.

span.quote: The critical electric field, in turn, scales approximately as the square of the semiconductor bandgap, so the BFOM scales approximately as the sixth power of the semiconductor bandgap. In other words, moving from GaN to AlN gives an increase in bandgap by a factor of 1.8 ≈ 6.0 eV/3.4 eV, but a nonlinear increase in the BFOM of ≈ 34 ≈ (1.8)6.

span.label: figures-of-merit
span.quote: Because many figures-of-merit for device performance scale nonlinearly with bandgap, these semiconductors have long been known to have compelling potential advantages over their narrower-bandgap cousins in high-power and RF electronics, as well as in deep-UV optoelectronics, quantum information, and extreme-environment applications.

span.label: Johnson figure of merit
span.quote: Note that for high-frequency high-power applications, the Johnson figure of merit (JFOM),23 which can be written as _v_ sat _E_ C/2π, where _v_ sat is the saturated carrier velocity, is more appropriate than the Baliga figure of merit.

span.quote: Note that for high-frequency high-power applications, the Johnson figure of merit (JFOM),23 which can be written as _v_ sat _E_ C/2π, where _v_ sat is the saturated carrier velocity, is more appropriate than the Baliga figure of merit.

span.label: permittivity
span.quote: Surprisingly for GaN there are at least five different sets of permittivity values in common use, and an important outcome of this study has been to establish the best values for GaN and AlN based on our thorough literature search and on recent measurements of AlN by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.

This tendency is illustrated in **Figure** **7** for n-type doping of AlGaN by Si. This problem restricts the possibility of the high-k dielectrics desirable for realizing high-performance UWBG MOSFETs in the future, and is an extremely important research opportunity/challenge.

The experimental thermal conductivity values of Ga2O3 fall in the range of ≈10–27 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature, which is one or two orders of magnitude lower than those of other UWBG semiconductors.

span.label: thermal conductivity
span.quote: Second, Ga2O3 has poor thermal conductivity and therefore poor heat-dissipation capability. This low thermal conductivity is perhaps the single most serious potential weakness of Ga2O3 for power devices. The experimental thermal conductivity values of Ga2O3 fall in the range of ≈10–27 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature, which is one or two orders of magnitude lower than those of other UWBG semiconductors.

span.quote: Doping of AlN is still in its infancy, with no known acceptors available and sulfur postulated as the only likely shallow donor.

span.label: Hall mobilities
span.quote: Finally, in several instances in the table the reported mobilities are Hall mobilities, as the Hall conversion factor is unknown for those materials.

span.label: bandgap → dielectric constant
span.note: AN INVERSE TRADE-OFF ACROSS MATERIALS, NOT A CAUSAL EFFECT WITHIN ONE. `any dielectric with a large bandgap will tend to have a low dielectric constant - and vice versa`. Nothing is being done to a bandgap to lower a permittivity; it is a regularity over the space of available materials, and it is the reason a high-k ultrawide-bandgap gate insulator may not exist. `causes ... reduces` would assert a mechanism the paper does not claim, and there is no `trades-off-against` or `correlates-with` type
span.quote: The most fundamental obstacle is that any dielectric with a large bandgap will tend to have a low dielectric constant—and vice versa. This problem restricts the possibility of the high-k dielectrics desirable for realizing high-performance UWBG MOSFETs in the future, and is an extremely important research opportunity/challenge.

span.label: AlN → acceptors
span.note: A MATERIAL DEFINED HERE BY WHAT IT LACKS. `no known acceptors available and sulfur postulated as the only likely shallow donor` - this is the single fact that keeps AlN out of bipolar devices, and every one of the eight relation types asserts that something HOLDS. The nearest available edge, `causes ... eliminates`, says AlN does something to acceptors; what is true is that none has been found
span.quote: Doping of AlN is still in its infancy, with no known acceptors available and sulfur postulated as the only likely shallow donor.

span.label: maturity → Ga2O3
span.note: A JUDGEMENT ABOUT A THING, MADE BY THE PAPER, AND LABELLED AS ONE. `an informal assessment of the maturity level`, resolving to Mature or Immature over three named sub-criteria. This is the relation type this corpus most needs and does not have - an ASSESSMENT edge, carrying who judged, on what criteria, and how firmly. Every one of our eight types says something about the world; none says something about an appraisal of the world
span.quote: Finally, based on the current state-of-the-art values for their properties, we give an informal assessment of the maturity level of the various materials.

span.label: maturity assessment - THE PAPER CALLS ITS OWN JUDGEMENT LAYER INFORMAL, IN THE SENTENCE THAT INTRODUCES IT. It is a Mature/Immature verdict resting on three named sub-criteria - doping, volume/cost, substrate size and availability - each reported separately in its own table row. A score whose inputs are printed beside it is a score a reader can disagree with
span.quote: Finally, based on the current state-of-the-art values for their properties, we give an informal assessment of the maturity level of the various materials.

span.label: figure of merit - THERE IS NO SINGLE ONE, AND WHICH APPLIES DEPENDS ON THE APPLICATION. The Baliga FOM is for low-frequency unipolar vertical power switches; for high-frequency high-power work the Johnson FOM is `more appropriate`. A material's rank changes with the question, so a table of FOMs is a table of conditional rankings
span.quote: Note that for high-frequency high-power applications, the Johnson figure of merit (JFOM),23 which can be written as _v_ sat _E_ C/2π, where _v_ sat is the saturated carrier velocity, is more appropriate than the Baliga figure of merit.

span.label: critical electric field, in the properties table - PROJECTED, NOT MEASURED. The values for AlN, Ga2O3, c-BN and diamond are calculated from GaN's experimentally derived field, and to compare them fairly the authors assume the SAME hypothetical device for all: a non-punched-through p+/n diode at a stated donor concentration. A number in a properties column that is a model output with a device baked into it
span.quote: The second materials/device properties row reports projected bulk values of the critical electric field ( _E_ C) at avalanche breakdown for each UWBG material starting with AlN (the HEMT column is a measured result). The projection uses the experimentally derived _E_ C for GaN59 as the baseline (corrected for the updated values of mobility and permittivity in the table), as this is the highest known _E_ C for any GaN or SiC diode. These projections follow the method described in detail in Hollis and Kaplar,60 and, to ensure a level playing field for all materials, assume a non-punched-through p+/n diode having an ionized donor concentration of 1016 cm−3 in the n-region.

span.label: intrinsic carrier concentration, for an ultrawide-bandgap material - A NUMBER FERMI-DIRAC STATISTICS PRODUCE THAT IS NOT A QUANTITY. Around 10^-10 cm^-3, which the authors say `has no direct physical meaning`, because the statistics assume carriers come from the high-energy tail of a thermal distribution and that assumption fails several electron-volts from a band edge. It still enters TCAD models and destabilises them
span.quote: In UWBG materials, Fermi–Dirac statistics predict they are theoretically 10−10 cm−3 or less for intrinsic material, a concentration that has no direct physical meaning.

span.label: immature - THE PAPER'S VERDICT ON EVERY UWBG MATERIAL INCLUDING THE ONES IT CHAMPIONS, and it is a comparative claim rather than a criticism: the field is placed where GaN and SiC were in the 1980s. Each of the three leading materials is poor on at least one of the three metrics, and the paper says which
span.quote: One can see that each of the three UWBG materials presently has poor performance in their states-of-the-art in at least one of the three important metrics: AlN and Ga2O3 cannot (or can only poorly) be p-doped; and diamond has limited size or relatively poor quality substrates.

span.label: material property, of the kind tabulated in reviews - NOT NECESSARILY STABLE. This paper re-derived them because values in common use were measured decades ago on material that would now be called highly defective. GaN turned out to have at least FIVE different permittivity sets in circulation, and AlN's bandgap was moved from 6.2 to 6.0 eV in 2010 by a better measurement. A constant in a table has a date and a method behind it
span.quote: Surprisingly for GaN there are at least five different sets of permittivity values in common use, and an important outcome of this study has been to establish the best values for GaN and AlN based on our thorough literature search and on recent measurements of AlN by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.

span.label: critiques → the material property values in common use across the semiconductor literature, including for GaN, many measured decades ago on highly defective material
span.quote: It was necessitated in part by the fact that many material properties in common use (even for GaN) were determined by measurements performed decades ago on material that was highly defective by today's standards.

span.label: distinguishes-from → the five different sets of GaN permittivity values circulating in the field
span.note: the paper does not adjudicate between the five on theoretical grounds - it re-searches the literature and takes new AlN measurements, and calls establishing the best values an important outcome OF THIS STUDY rather than a side note
span.quote: Surprisingly for GaN there are at least five different sets of permittivity values in common use, and an important outcome of this study has been to establish the best values for GaN and AlN based on our thorough literature search and on recent measurements of AlN by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.

span.label: contradicts → the historical 6.2 eV bandgap of AlN, based on older absorption measurements
span.note: not this paper's own finding - it reports the 2010 redefinition by high-resolution photoluminescence and adopts it. The relation is to the superseded value
span.quote: The first materials/device properties row lists bandgaps, as generally accepted by the community for some time, with the exception of AlN whose “historical” bandgap of 6.2 eV (based on older absorption measurements) was redefined more accurately in 2010 to ≈6.0 eV using high-resolution photoluminescence.

span.quote: Thus, the UWBG semiconductors currently find themselves at a stage of development similar to that of the WBG semiconductors GaN and SiC in the 1980s—emerging materials with many research challenges, but also with opportunities for orders-of-magnitude improvement in performance both for existing applications and for application domains heretofore considered impossible to address.

span.quote: Surprisingly for GaN there are at least five different sets of permittivity values in common use, and an important outcome of this study has been to establish the best values for GaN and AlN based on our thorough literature search and on recent measurements of AlN by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.

span.quote: The first materials/device properties row lists bandgaps, as generally accepted by the community for some time, with the exception of AlN whose “historical” bandgap of 6.2 eV (based on older absorption measurements) was redefined more accurately in 2010 to ≈6.0 eV using high-resolution photoluminescence.

span.label: the critical breakdown fields of AlN, BN, Ga2O3 and diamond - the property the entire case rests on - have not been accurately determined
span.quote: While critical breakdown fields in GaN have been measured59, 60 to be in excess of ≈4 MV cm−1, those in AlN, BN, Ga2O3, and diamond are yet to be accurately determined.

span.label: ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor = one whose bandgap is significantly wider than GaN's 3.4 eV
span.quote: Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors, with bandgaps significantly wider than the 3.4 eV of GaN, represent an exciting and challenging new area of research in semiconductor materials, physics, devices, and applications.

span.label: Baliga figure of merit = breakdown voltage squared over specific on-resistance, for a low-frequency unipolar vertical power switch
span.quote: For example, in the simple case of a low-frequency unipolar vertical power switch, the widely used Baliga figure of merit (BFOM)22 is defined as _V_ 2BR/ _R_ ON-SP. Here, _V_ BR is the breakdown voltage (the maximum voltage the switch can block when it is off), and _R_ ON-SP is the specific on-resistance (the inverse of the conductance per unit area when the switch is on).

span.quote: The last few rows, 9 and 9a–9c, of Table 2 comprise a materials maturity assessment across the categories of doping, volume/cost, and substrate size/availability, with an overall assessment of “Mature” or “Immature.”

span.label: the three obstacles to doping a wide-gap material: ionization energies rise with bandgap, carriers self-trap, and dopants are compensated
span.quote: This is in part due to the presence of three obstacles not present in the traditional narrower gap semiconductors. The first is the fact that most dopant ionization energies increase with bandgap. As ionization energy increases, the fraction of carriers that are thermodynamically “activated” from bound to free states decreases, making it difficult to achieve the UWBG free carrier concentrations at room temperature necessary for many devices.

span.label: moving from GaN to AlN raises the bandgap by 1.8x and the Baliga figure of merit by about 34x - the sixth power of that ratio
span.quote: The critical electric field, in turn, scales approximately as the square of the semiconductor bandgap, so the BFOM scales approximately as the sixth power of the semiconductor bandgap. In other words, moving from GaN to AlN gives an increase in bandgap by a factor of 1.8 ≈ 6.0 eV/3.4 eV, but a nonlinear increase in the BFOM of ≈ 34 ≈ (1.8)6.

span.label: breakdown voltage scales as the 4th power of bandgap, since the critical field goes as its square
span.quote: and _E_ c scales as the 2nd power of _E_ G,225 _V_ BR of a semiconductor switch scales as the 4th power of _E_ G.
